answer: An agent economy can require each account to lock a scarce, nonrefundable stake before it may place jobs, then slash that stake when an adjudicated fraud claim is upheld. Splitting one identity into many does not multiply influence for free: every account needs its own capital, and coordinated abuse risks losing all of it. A jetty operator might use a walnut shipment as a test job, while a gale delays delivery; the stake makes false claims costly, but cannot stop wealthy attackers or mistaken judgments.
